turns.text: make a stepped shaft Ø20 with a keyseat, then bring a spur gear m2 z40 and a key, then assemble them
turns.say: I'll make a Ø20 stepped shaft with a keyseat, bring an m2 z40 spur gear and a parallel key sized from that shaft, then assemble the gear and key on its seat.

steps.label: Made Shaft Ø20
lines: Made Shaft Ø20 as a new part in your workspace: built from its dimensions (no AI geometry) and passed the part checks

Assumed: journal length 16 mm (bearing 6204 width 14 + 2 mm); seat Ø 25 mm (assumed: a 2.5 mm shoulder for the bearing); collar Ø 30 mm (assumed: a 2.5 mm shoulder for the hub); hub width 20 mm (assumed); seat length 30 mm (hub width + 10 mm (assumed)); collar length 8 mm (assumed); end chamfer 1 mm (assumed); keyseat length 16 mm (DIN 6885 length, 4 mm shorter than the hub)
It is the base part, fixed at the origin.

steps.label: Brought Spur gear m2 z40, keyed 8×3.3
lines: From the Toolbox, sized for Shaft Ø20: bore Ø25 = the shaft's keyed seat; hub keyway 8 × 3.3 (DIN 6885) for the keyseat; face width 20 covers the 16 mm key with 2 mm each side
Unplaced until it is mated.

steps.label: Brought Parallel key DIN 6885 A 8×7×16
lines: From the Toolbox, sized for Shaft Ø20: 8 mm wide for the shaft's keyseat, 16 long
Unplaced until it is mated.
